sentences.zh: 南琛巡洋艦、南瑞巡洋艦，又名運送艦。

translations.literal: Nanchen and Nanrui cruisers, also called transport ships.
translations.idiomatic: The cruisers Nanchen and Nanrui, also known as transport ships.

sentences.zh: 光緒九年，兩江總督左宗棠由德國伏爾鏗廠訂購。

translations.literal: Guangxu year 9, ordered from the German Vulcan works by Liangjiang governor-general Zuo Zongtang.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered from Vulcan by Zuo Zongtang in Guangxu 9.

sentences.zh: 知福龍魚雷艇，光緒十二年，由德國訂購。

translations.literal: Zhifulong torpedo boat—Guangxu year 12, ordered from Germany.
translations.idiomatic: The torpedo boat Zhifulong: ordered from Germany in Guangxu 12.

sentences.zh: 十六年隸北洋海軍。

translations.literal: Year 16 attached to the Beiyang Navy.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year she was attached to the Beiyang Navy.

sentences.zh: 致遠巡洋艦、靖遠巡洋艦，光緒十二年，由英國訂購，船價及砲位，凡銀一百六十九萬有奇。

translations.literal: Zhiyuan and Jingyuan cruisers—Guangxu year 12, ordered from Britain, ship price and gun mounts together totaling a little over one million six hundred ninety thousand taels of silver.
translations.idiomatic: The cruisers Zhiyuan and Jingyuan: ordered from Britain in Guangxu 12 for a little over one million six hundred ninety thousand taels including guns.

sentences.zh: 經遠巡洋艦、來遠巡洋艦，光緒十二年，由德國訂購，船價及砲位，凡銀一百七十三萬有奇。

translations.literal: Jingyuan and Laiyuan cruisers—Guangxu year 12, ordered from Germany, ship price and gun mounts together totaling a little over one million seven hundred thirty thousand taels of silver.
translations.idiomatic: The cruisers Jingyuan and Laiyuan: ordered from Germany in Guangxu 12 for a little over one million seven hundred thirty thousand taels including guns.

sentences.zh: 光緒十三、四年，與致遠、靖遠先後到華，均隸北洋海軍。

translations.literal: Guangxu years 13 and 14, arrived in China in succession with the Zhiyuan and Jingyuan, all attached to the Beiyang Navy.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 13–14 they reached China after the Zhiyuan and Jingyuan and joined the Beiyang Navy.

sentences.zh: 左隊一號魚雷大快艇，光緒十二年，直隸總督李鴻章由英國百濟公司訂購，價銀八萬有奇，十三年到華。

translations.literal: Left Squadron No. 1 great torpedo launch—Guangxu year 12, ordered from the British Baiji company by Zhili governor-general Li Hongzhang, price a little over eighty thousand taels of silver, arrived in Guangxu year 13.
translations.idiomatic: Left Squadron No. 1 torpedo launch: ordered from the British Baiji company by Li Hongzhang in Guangxu 12 for a little over eighty thousand taels; arrived in Guangxu 13.

sentences.zh: 左隊二號魚雷大快艇、左隊三號魚雷大快艇、右隊一號魚雷大快艇、右隊二號魚雷大快艇、右隊三號魚雷大快艇，以上魚雷艇六艘，光緒十二、三年，先後由德國船廠購買材料，到華配合，以德員教授。

translations.literal: Left Squadron Nos. 2 and 3, Right Squadron Nos. 1, 2, and 3 great torpedo launches—the above six torpedo boats, Guangxu years 12 and 13, materials successively purchased from a German shipyard and assembled in China, with German instructors teaching.
translations.idiomatic: Left Squadron Nos. 2 and 3 and Right Squadron Nos. 1, 2, and 3—six torpedo boats in all: in Guangxu 12–13 materials were bought from German yards, assembled in China, and German instructors were employed.

sentences.zh: 辰字魚雷艇、宿字魚雷艇，由德國伏爾鏗廠訂購，光緒二十一年到華。

translations.literal: Chen and Su torpedo boats—ordered from the German Vulcan works, arrived in China in Guangxu year 21.
translations.idiomatic: The torpedo boats Chen and Su: ordered from Vulcan and arrived in Guangxu 21.

sentences.zh: 列字魚雷艇、張字魚雷艇，由德石效廠訂購，光緒二十一年到華。

translations.literal: Lie and Zhang torpedo boats—ordered from the German Schichau works, arrived in China in Guangxu year 21.
translations.idiomatic: The torpedo boats Lie and Zhang: ordered from Germany's Schichau works and arrived in Guangxu 21.

sentences.zh: 福安砲艦，光緒二十年，由英國阿摩士庄廠訂購。

translations.literal: Fu'an gunboat—Guangxu year 20, ordered from the British Armstrong works.
translations.idiomatic: The gunboat Fu'an: ordered from Armstrong in Guangxu 20.

sentences.zh: 飛霆驅逐艦，光緒二十一年，由英國阿摩士庄廠訂購。

translations.literal: Feiting destroyer—Guangxu year 21, ordered from the British Armstrong works.
translations.idiomatic: The destroyer Feiting: ordered from Armstrong in Guangxu 21.

sentences.zh: 飛鷹驅逐艦，光緒二十二年，由德國伏爾鏗廠訂購。

translations.literal: Feiying destroyer—Guangxu year 22, ordered from the German Vulcan works.
translations.idiomatic: The destroyer Feiying: ordered from Vulcan in Guangxu 22.

sentences.zh: 海天巡洋艦、海圻巡洋艦，即穹甲快船。

translations.literal: The Haitian and Haiqi cruisers were protected cruisers.
translations.idiomatic: The cruisers Haitian and Haiqi were protected cruisers.

sentences.zh: 光緒二十二年，由總稅務司在英國阿摩士庄廠訂購，每艘價值三十二萬八千二百四十二鎊。

translations.literal: Guangxu year 22, ordered from the British Armstrong works by the Inspector General of Customs, each ship valued at three hundred twenty-eight thousand two hundred forty-two pounds sterling.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 22 the Inspector General of Customs ordered them from Armstrong in Britain at three hundred twenty-eight thousand two hundred forty-two pounds each.

sentences.zh: 古海籌巡洋艦、海容巡洋艦、海琛巡洋艦，光緒二十二年，由總理衙門在德國伏爾鏗廠訂購，每艘價值十六萬三千鎊。

translations.literal: The former Haichou cruiser and the Hairong and Haichen cruisers—Guangxu year 22, ordered from the German Vulcan works by the Zongli Yamen, each ship valued at one hundred sixty-three thousand pounds sterling.
translations.idiomatic: The cruisers Haichou, Hairong, and Haichen: ordered from Germany's Vulcan works by the Zongli Yamen in Guangxu 22 at one hundred sixty-three thousand pounds each.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，與海天、海圻巡洋艦先後到華。

translations.literal: Year 24, they arrived in China one after another together with the Haitian and Haiqi cruisers.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year they reached China in succession, along with the Haitian and Haiqi.

sentences.zh: 江元砲艦、江亨砲艦、江利砲艦、江貞砲艦，由兩江總督在日本川畸廠訂購。

translations.literal: The Jiangyuan, Jiangheng, Jiangli, and Jiangzhen gunboats were ordered from the Japanese Kawasaki works by the Liangjiang governor-general.
translations.idiomatic: The gunboats Jiangyuan, Jiangheng, Jiangli, and Jiangzhen were ordered from Kawasaki in Japan by the Liangjiang governor-general.

sentences.zh: 江元於光緒三十三年告成。

translations.literal: The Jiangyuan was completed in Guangxu year 33.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiangyuan was completed in Guangxu 33.

sentences.zh: 江亨於三十四年告成。

translations.literal: The Jiangheng was completed in year 34.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiangheng was completed in the thirty-fourth year.

sentences.zh: 江利、江貞於宣統元年告成。

translations.literal: The Jiangli and Jiangzhen were completed in the first year of Xuantong.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiangli and Jiangzhen were completed in Xuantong 1.

sentences.zh: 先造一艘，價日本金三十一萬五千元。

translations.literal: The first ship built cost three hundred fifteen thousand Japanese yen.
translations.idiomatic: The first vessel cost three hundred fifteen thousand yen.

sentences.zh: 續造三艘，每艘價日本金二十九萬三百二十五元。

translations.literal: Three more were built afterward, each priced at two hundred ninety thousand three hundred twenty-five Japanese yen.
translations.idiomatic: Three more followed, each at two hundred ninety thousand three hundred twenty-five yen.

sentences.zh: 湖鵬魚雷艇、湖鶚魚雷艇、湖鷹魚雷艇、湖隼魚雷艇，由湖廣總督張之洞在日本川畸廠訂購。

translations.literal: The Hupeng, Hu'e, Huying, and Hun torpedo boats were ordered from the Japanese Kawasaki works by Huguang governor-general Zhang Zhidong.
translations.idiomatic: The torpedo boats Hupeng, Hu'e, Huying, and Hun were ordered from Kawasaki by Zhang Zhidong, governor-general of Huguang.

sentences.zh: 湖鵬、湖鶚二艇，於光緒三十三年到華。

translations.literal: The two boats Hupeng and Hu'e arrived in China in Guangxu year 33.
translations.idiomatic: The Hupeng and Hu'e reached China in Guangxu 33.

sentences.zh: 湖鷹、湖隼二艇，於三十四年到華。

translations.literal: The two boats Huying and Hun arrived in China in year 34.
translations.idiomatic: The Huying and Hun arrived in the thirty-fourth year.

sentences.zh: 每艘合日本金三十八萬元。

translations.literal: Each ship totaled three hundred eighty thousand Japanese yen.
translations.idiomatic: Each cost three hundred eighty thousand yen.

sentences.zh: 楚泰砲艦、楚同砲艦、楚豫砲艦、楚有砲鑒、楚觀砲艦、楚謙砲艦，均航海砲艦。

translations.literal: The Chutai, Chutong, Chuyu, Chu You, Chuguan, and Chuqian gunboats were all seagoing gunboats.
translations.idiomatic: The seagoing gunboats Chutai, Chutong, Chuyu, Chu You, Chuguan, and Chuqian.

sentences.zh: 由湖廣總督張之洞在日本川畸廠訂購。

translations.literal: They were ordered from the Japanese Kawasaki works by Huguang governor-general Zhang Zhidong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhidong ordered them from Kawasaki in Japan.

sentences.zh: 楚同、楚泰、楚有三砲艦，於光緒三十三年二月到華。

translations.literal: The three gunboats Chutong, Chutai, and Chu You arrived in China in the second month of Guangxu year 33.
translations.idiomatic: Chutong, Chutai, and Chu You reached China in the second month of Guangxu 33.

sentences.zh: 楚豫、楚觀、楚謙三砲艦，於十月到華。

translations.literal: The three gunboats Chuyu, Chuguan, and Chuqian arrived in China in the tenth month.
translations.idiomatic: Chuyu, Chuguan, and Chuqian arrived in the tenth month.

sentences.zh: 每艘合日本金四十五萬五千元。

translations.literal: Each ship totaled four hundred fifty-five thousand Japanese yen.
translations.idiomatic: Each cost four hundred fifty-five thousand yen.

sentences.zh: 海龍魚雷艇、海青魚雷艇、海華魚雷艇、海犀魚雷艇，在德國實碩廠訂購，於光緒三十四年到華。

translations.literal: The Hailong, Haiqing, Haihua, and Haixi torpedo boats were ordered from the German Schichau works and arrived in China in Guangxu year 34.
translations.idiomatic: The torpedo boats Hailong, Haiqing, Haihua, and Haixi were ordered from Schichau in Germany and reached China in Guangxu 34.

sentences.zh: 舞鳳航海砲艦，宣統三年，在青島德國船廠訂購。

translations.literal: The Wufeng seagoing gunboat—Xuantong year 3, ordered from a German shipyard at Qingdao.
translations.idiomatic: The seagoing gunboat Wufeng: ordered from a German yard at Qingdao in Xuantong 3.

sentences.zh: 江犀砲艦、江鯤砲艦，均淺水砲艦，原名新璧、新珍。

translations.literal: The Jiangxi and Jiangkun gunboats were both shallow-draft gunboats, originally named Xinbi and Xinzhen.
translations.idiomatic: The shallow-draft gunboats Jiangxi and Jiangkun had originally been named Xinbi and Xinzhen.

sentences.zh: 江犀艦在德國克魯伯廠訂購，江鯤艦在德國伏爾鏗廠訂購，均以材料運華，宣統三年，在江南造船所配合，每艘價值一萬八千九百八十鎊。

translations.literal: The Jiangxi was ordered from the German Krupp works and the Jiangkun from the German Vulcan works; materials for both were shipped to China, and in Xuantong year 3 they were assembled at the Jiangnan shipyard, each ship valued at eighteen thousand nine hundred eighty pounds sterling.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiangxi was ordered from Krupp and the Jiangkun from Vulcan; their materials were sent to China and assembled at the Jiangnan shipyard in Xuantong 3, at eighteen thousand nine hundred eighty pounds each.

sentences.zh: 古肇和巡洋艦，宣統三年，在英國阿摩士庄廠訂購，價值二十一萬鎊。

translations.literal: The former Zhaohe cruiser—Xuantong year 3, ordered from the British Armstrong works, valued at two hundred ten thousand pounds sterling.
translations.idiomatic: The cruiser Zhaohe: ordered from Armstrong in Britain in Xuantong 3 for two hundred ten thousand pounds.

sentences.zh: 福州船廠，自造各兵艦。

translations.literal: The Fuzhou shipyard built its own warships.
translations.idiomatic: The Fuzhou shipyard built warships of its own.

sentences.zh: 始建船廠，聘工師於法，延教員於英。

translations.literal: When the yard was first established, engineers were hired from France and instructors invited from Britain.
translations.idiomatic: At its founding the yard hired engineers from France and instructors from Britain.

sentences.zh: 建船臺，購機器。

translations.literal: A building slip was constructed and machinery purchased.
translations.idiomatic: It built a slipway and bought machinery.

sentences.zh: 同治八年秋，第一號萬年清輪船成。

translations.literal: In the autumn of Tongzhi year 8, the first ship, the steamer Wannianqing, was completed.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of Tongzhi 8 the first vessel, the steamer Wannianqing, was launched.

sentences.zh: 十二年冬，華匠漸諳製造，廠機亦稍備，乃遣散洋員。

translations.literal: In the winter of year 12, Chinese craftsmen gradually mastered construction, the yard's machinery was also somewhat complete, and the foreign staff were then dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: By the winter of the twelfth year Chinese artisans had grown skilled, the yard's equipment was largely in place, and the foreign staff were sent home.

sentences.zh: 凡九年，成大小兵船、商船十五艘，成於洋員者十二，成於華匠者三。

translations.literal: Over nine years in all, fifteen large and small warships and merchant ships were completed—twelve by foreign staff and three by Chinese craftsmen.
translations.idiomatic: In nine years the yard completed fifteen warships and merchant vessels, twelve under foreign supervision and three by Chinese craftsmen alone.

sentences.zh: 光緒三年，始遣學生、藝徒至英、法二國留學。

translations.literal: Guangxu year 3, students and apprentices were first sent to study in Britain and France.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 3 the yard first sent students and apprentices to study in Britain and France.

sentences.zh: 六年歸國，製造、駕駛，悉以任之。

translations.literal: In year 6 they returned to China, and construction and navigation were entirely entrusted to them.
translations.idiomatic: They returned in the sixth year, and shipbuilding and sailing were placed wholly in their hands.

sentences.zh: 其製船之質，始皆以木，繼易木脅為鐵脅，易木板為鐵板，更進則純用鋼脅、鋼板，且護以鋼甲。

translations.literal: As for the materials used in shipbuilding, at first all were wood; then wooden ribs were replaced with iron ribs and wooden planking with iron plate; advancing further, steel ribs and steel plate were used exclusively, and armor plate was added for protection.
translations.idiomatic: Ships were first built entirely of wood, then wooden ribs gave way to iron ribs and wooden planking to iron plate; later still the yard used only steel ribs and steel plate, armored with steel plating.

sentences.zh: 船機則由立機改臥機。

translations.literal: Ship engines were changed from vertical to horizontal engines.
translations.idiomatic: Engines shifted from vertical to horizontal types.

sentences.zh: 船式則由常式為快船、為穹甲、為鋼甲。

translations.literal: Ship types progressed from conventional designs to fast cruisers, protected cruisers, and armored ships.
translations.idiomatic: Designs moved from conventional hulls to fast cruisers, protected cruisers, and armored warships.

sentences.zh: 至光緒三十三年，成船達四十艘。

translations.literal: By Guangxu year 33, completed ships reached forty vessels.
translations.idiomatic: By Guangxu 33 the yard had completed forty vessels.

translations.literal: The Guangdong shipyard built its own warships; Guangxu year 12, Liangguang governor-general Zhang Zhidong established a yard on the provincial river, selected and recruited Chinese workers, adopted plans from a British shipyard in Hong Kong, and built four shallow-draft gunboats named Guangyuan, Guangheng, Guangli, and Guangzhen.
translations.idiomatic: The Guangdong shipyard also built its own warships. In Guangxu 12 Zhang Zhidong established a yard on the provincial river, recruited Chinese workers, used plans from a British yard in Hong Kong, and built four shallow-draft gunboats: Guangyuan, Guangheng, Guangli, and Guangzhen.

sentences.zh: 直隸大沽船塢，自造拖船，遇順暗輪鋼拖船，光緒十四年造成，又守雷暗輪包鋼小輪船一艘，下雷暗輪包鋼小輪船一艘。

translations.literal: The Zhili Dagu dockyard built its own tugs: the Yushun, a screw steel tug completed in Guangxu year 14; also one small armored screw launch, Shoulei, and one small armored screw launch, Xialei.
translations.idiomatic: The Dagu dockyard in Zhili built tugs of its own, including the Yushun, a screw steel tug completed in Guangxu 14, plus the armored screw launches Shoulei and Xialei.

sentences.zh: 江南船廠，自造各兵艦。

translations.literal: The Jiangnan shipyard built its own warships.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiangnan shipyard built warships of its own.

sentences.zh: 咸豐十一年，曾國籓始有購買船砲及中國試造輪船之疏。

translations.literal: Xianfeng year 11, Zeng Guofan first submitted a memorial on purchasing ships and cannon and on China's trial construction of steamships.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianfeng 11 Zeng Guofan first memorialized the throne on buying ships and guns and on China's attempt to build steamships.

sentences.zh: 同治二年，於安慶設局，不用洋員，自造一小輪行駛。

translations.literal: Tongzhi year 2, a bureau was established at Anqing; without foreign staff, a small steamer was built and put into service.
translations.idiomatic: In Tongzhi 2 a bureau was set up at Anqing, and without foreign help it built a small steamer that actually ran.

sentences.zh: 令容閎出洋購買機器。

translations.literal: Rong Hong was ordered abroad to purchase machinery.
translations.idiomatic: Rong Hong was sent overseas to buy machinery.

sentences.zh: 四年，國籓於上海虹口奏設製造局。

translations.literal: Year 4, Guofan memorialized to establish a manufacturing bureau at Hongkou in Shanghai.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Guofan petitioned to establish a manufacturing bureau at Hongkou, Shanghai.

sentences.zh: 李鴻章撫蘇，偕丁日昌於上海鐵廠專造槍砲，以供征伐。

translations.literal: Li Hongzhang governed Jiangsu and, together with Ding Richang, devoted the Shanghai ironworks exclusively to making muskets and cannon for the campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: While Li Hongzhang governed Jiangsu, he and Ding Richang used the Shanghai ironworks solely to cast muskets and cannon for the war effort.

sentences.zh: 六年四月，國籓疏請撥留洋稅一成，為專造輪船之用。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of year 6, Guofan memorialized requesting that one-tenth of the maritime customs revenue be set aside exclusively for building steamships.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the sixth year Guofan asked that one-tenth of customs revenue be reserved solely for building steamships.

sentences.zh: 汽爐、機器、船殼三者，咸研究圖說，自出機杼。

translations.literal: Boilers, machinery, and hulls—all three were studied from plans and worked out independently.
translations.idiomatic: Boilers, engines, and hulls were all studied from plans and developed on their own designs.

sentences.zh: 先造汽爐廠、機器廠、熟鐵廠、洋槍樓、木工廠、鑄銅鐵廠、火箭廠、庫房、棧房、工務房、工匠室，以應要需。

translations.literal: First were built a boiler shop, machine shop, wrought-iron shop, foreign-style musket hall, carpentry shop, bronze- and iron-casting shop, rocket shop, warehouses, storage sheds, engineering offices, and workers' quarters to meet requirements.
translations.idiomatic: First came a boiler shop, machine shop, wrought-iron shop, musket hall, carpentry shop, foundry, rocket shop, warehouses, storage sheds, engineering offices, and workers' quarters.

sentences.zh: 復築船塢以整破舟，建瓦棚以儲材料，立學館以譯圖說。

translations.literal: A dry dock was also built to repair damaged vessels, tiled sheds erected to store materials, and a school established to translate plans.
translations.idiomatic: A dry dock was added to repair damaged hulls, tiled sheds to store materials, and a school to translate technical drawings.

sentences.zh: 建築既堅，規模亦肅。

translations.literal: The buildings were solid and the layout imposing.
translations.idiomatic: The buildings were solid and the layout orderly and imposing.

sentences.zh: 同治六年，李鴻章建江南製造局，從事製船。

translations.literal: Tongzhi year 6, Li Hongzhang established the Jiangnan Manufacturing Bureau and undertook shipbuilding.
translations.idiomatic: In Tongzhi 6 Li Hongzhang founded the Jiangnan Manufacturing Bureau and turned to building ships.

sentences.zh: 八年，測海、操江兩兵船製成。

translations.literal: Year 8, the two warships Cehai and Caojiang were completed.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year the warships Cehai and Caojiang were completed.

sentences.zh: 九年，威靖兵船成。

translations.literal: Year 9, the warship Weijing was completed.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year the warship Weijing was launched.

sentences.zh: 以萬金購德國船為練船之用。

translations.literal: Ten thousand taels of gold were spent to purchase a German ship for use as a training vessel.
translations.idiomatic: Ten thousand taels in gold bought a German vessel for training duty.

sentences.zh: 十二年，海安兵船製成。

translations.literal: Year 12, the warship Hai'an was completed.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year the warship Hai'an was completed.

sentences.zh: 光緒元年，馭遠兵船製成。

translations.literal: Guangxu year 1, the warship Yuyuan was completed.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 1 the warship Yuyuan was completed.

sentences.zh: 二年，金甌小鐵甲船製成。

translations.literal: Year 2, the small ironclad Jin'ou was completed.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year the small ironclad Jin'ou was launched.

sentences.zh: 五年，兩江總督沈葆楨疏言：「江南船廠所製兵船，五百匹馬力以下者五艘，其兵數餉章，與福州所造各兵船相等。

translations.literal: Year 5, Liangjiang governor-general Shen Baozhen memorialized: "Of the warships built by the Jiangnan shipyard, five were of less than five hundred horsepower; their complements and pay scales were equal to those of the various warships built at Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year Liangjiang governor-general Shen Baozhen wrote: "The Jiangnan yard had built five warships of under five hundred horsepower, with complements and pay scales matching those of Fuzhou-built vessels.

sentences.zh: 」八年，購外洋商船一艘，改造為防緝之用，名曰鈞和。

translations.literal: " Year 8, one foreign merchant ship was purchased and converted for patrol and interdiction, named Junhe.
translations.idiomatic: " In the eighth year a foreign merchantman was bought, converted for patrol duty, and named Junhe.

sentences.zh: 嗣後未有造作。

translations.literal: Afterward no further construction was undertaken.
translations.idiomatic: No further building followed.

sentences.zh: 光緒三十年，南洋大臣周馥等，以南洋近年以來，舊有兵船，日益窳朽，徒糜餉項，無裨實際，亟應分別裁留，認真整理。

translations.literal: Guangxu year 30, the Nanyang governor Zhou Fu and others, noting that in recent years the Nanyang Fleet's existing warships had grown daily more decayed, wasting pay funds without practical benefit, urgently needed to be selectively retained or cut and conscientiously reorganized.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 30 Zhou Fu and other Nanyang officials reported that the fleet's old warships had grown ever more rotten, wasting funds without serving any real purpose, and urgently needed selective retention, cuts, and thorough reorganization.

sentences.zh: 非定章程，不能革除舊習；

translations.literal: Without fixed regulations, old abuses could not be abolished;
translations.idiomatic: Without firm regulations the old abuses could not be uprooted;

sentences.zh: 非專派大員督辦，不能造就將才。

translations.literal: Without specially appointing a high official to supervise, naval commanders could not be trained.
translations.idiomatic: Only by appointing a senior officer to oversee the work could the navy train real commanders.

sentences.zh: 因奏派現統北洋海軍廣東水師提督葉祖珪督辦南洋水師學堂、上海船塢，凡餉械支應一切事宜，有與海軍相關者，均歸考核。

translations.literal: He therefore memorialized appointing Ye Zugui, presently commanding the Beiyang Navy as Guangdong Naval Commander, to supervise the Nanyang Naval Academy and the Shanghai dry dock; all matters of pay, arms, supplies, and anything related to the navy were placed under his inspection.
translations.idiomatic: He recommended Ye Zugui—who already commanded the Beiyang Fleet as Guangdong naval commander—to run the Nanyang Naval Academy and the Shanghai dry dock, with authority over every naval matter of pay, arms, and supply.

sentences.zh: 嗣復奏稱江南製造機器總局內舊有船塢，本為製造官商輪船並修理船械而設，日久弊生，多糜經費，而辦理之員，類無造船專門之學，以致承修船隻，工價高昂。

translations.literal: He later memorialized again that the old dry dock within the Jiangnan Machine Works had been established to build official and merchant steamers and repair naval craft; over time abuses arose, funds were wasted, and those in charge generally lacked specialized training in shipbuilding, so repair prices for vessels were exorbitant.
translations.idiomatic: He later reported that the Jiangnan arsenal's old dry dock, meant to build government and merchant steamers and repair warships, had grown corrupt and costly; managers without real shipbuilding training charged exorbitant repair fees.

sentences.zh: 近年以來，商船裹足不前，兵船反入洋塢，非認真整理，無由振興。

translations.literal: In recent years merchant shipping had held back, while men-of-war went instead to foreign docks; without earnest reorganization there was no way to revive the yard.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years merchant work had dried up while warships were sent to foreign yards; nothing would improve without a thorough overhaul.

sentences.zh: 經與北洋大臣會商，定議船塢別簡大員經理，仿商塢辦法，掃除舊習，妥籌改良船塢，與海軍事相表裡。

translations.literal: After consultation with the Beiyang minister, it was decided to appoint a separate high official to manage the dock, following commercial dock practice, sweeping away old abuses, and properly planning improvements so the dock and naval affairs would support each other.
translations.idiomatic: After talks with the Beiyang minister, they agreed to put the dock under its own senior manager, run it like a commercial yard, root out old abuses, and rebuild it as the navy's industrial partner.

sentences.zh: 廣東水師提督葉祖珪，系總理南北洋海軍，往來津、滬，則上海船塢事宜，自應歸其督察，以一事權。

translations.literal: Guangdong Naval Commander Ye Zugui, who oversaw both Beiyang and Nanyang navies and traveled between Tianjin and Shanghai, should naturally supervise Shanghai dock affairs to unify authority.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Zugui, who commanded both northern and southern fleets and shuttled between Tianjin and Shanghai, should supervise the Shanghai dock to keep authority in one hand.

sentences.zh: 遂將船塢與製造局劃分，名曰江南船塢，製造局歸陸軍部轄，船塢歸海軍部轄，以專責任。

translations.literal: The dock was therefore separated from the manufacturing bureau and named the Jiangnan Shipyard; the bureau came under the Army Ministry and the dock under the Navy Ministry, each with its own responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: The dock was split off as the Jiangnan Shipyard: the arsenal went to the Army Ministry and the dock to the Navy Ministry, each with a clear mandate.

sentences.zh: 此後製造復興，三十四年，甘泉、安豐二兵船成。

translations.literal: Thereafter construction revived; in the thirty-fourth year the men-of-war Ganquan and Anfeng were completed.
translations.idiomatic: Building revived afterward; in the thirty-fourth year [Guangxu, 1908] the Ganquan and Anfeng were launched.

sentences.zh: 宣統二年，聯鯨兵船成。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xuantong the men-of-war Lianjing was completed.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuantong 2 [1910] the Lianjing was finished.

sentences.zh: 三年，澄海砲船成。

translations.literal: In the third year the gunboat Chenghai was completed.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year [Xuantong, 1911] the gunboat Chenghai was completed.

sentences.zh: 海軍自甲午戰後，所餘南洋各艦，不復成軍。

translations.literal: After the navy since the jiawu war, the remaining Nanyang vessels no longer formed a fleet.
translations.idiomatic: After the war of 1894–95, what was left of the southern fleet no longer counted as a real navy.

sentences.zh: 嗣後逐漸購置，其編製非復北洋舊章。

translations.literal: Thereafter ships were gradually purchased, and the organization no longer followed the old Beiyang regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Ships were bought back piecemeal, and the organization no longer followed Beiyang practice.

sentences.zh: 每艦設艦長一員，副長一員，協長一員，航海正一員，航海副一員或二員，槍砲正一員，槍砲副一員或二員，魚雷正、魚雷副一員或二員，輪機長一員，輪機正一員或二員，輪機副一員至八員，軍需正一員，軍需副一員或二員，軍醫正一員，軍醫副一員或二員，書記官一員。

translations.literal: Each ship had one captain, one executive officer, one assistant executive officer, one navigation lieutenant, one or two assistant navigation officers, one gunnery lieutenant, one or two assistant gunnery officers, one or two torpedo lieutenants and assistants, one chief engineer, one or two senior engineers, one to eight assistant engineers, one supply officer, one or two assistant supply officers, one medical officer, one or two assistant medical officers, and one secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Each vessel carried a captain, executive and assistant executive officers, navigation and gunnery officers with assistants, torpedo officers, a chief engineer with up to eight assistants, supply and medical staff with assistants, and a secretary.

sentences.zh: 其戰艦約分新舊二類，新式而有武力者，巡洋艦四，曰海圻、四千三百頓。

translations.literal: Warships were roughly divided into new and old types; among the new and combat-capable were four cruisers: Haiqi, four thousand three hundred tons.
translations.idiomatic: Warships fell roughly into new and old categories. Among the modern fighting ships were four cruisers, beginning with the Haiqi at 4,300 tons.

sentences.zh: 曰海容、曰海琛、曰海籌。

translations.literal: Named Hairong, Haichen, and Haichou.
translations.idiomatic: The Hairong, Haichen, and Haichou.

sentences.zh: 各二千九百五十頓。

translations.literal: Each two thousand nine hundred fifty tons.
translations.idiomatic: Each 2,950 tons.

sentences.zh: 砲艦十一，曰楚泰、曰楚謙、曰楚觀、曰楚豫、曰楚有、曰楚同、各七百八十頓。

translations.literal: Eleven gunboats: Chutai, Chuqian, Chuguan, Chuyu, Chuyou, and Chutong, each seven hundred eighty tons.
translations.idiomatic: Eleven gunboats—the Chutai, Chuqian, Chuguan, Chuyu, Chuyou, and Chutong—each 780 tons.

sentences.zh: 曰江元、曰江亨、曰江利、曰江貞、曰江鏡。

translations.literal: Named Jiangyuan, Jiangheng, Jiangli, Jiangzhen, and Jiangjing.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiangyuan, Jiangheng, Jiangli, Jiangzhen, and Jiangjing.

sentences.zh: 各五百頓。

translations.literal: Each five hundred tons.
translations.idiomatic: Each 500 tons.

sentences.zh: 水雷砲艦一，曰飛鷹。

translations.literal: One mine gunboat named Feiying.
translations.idiomatic: One mine gunboat, the Feiying.

sentences.zh: 八百五十頓。

translations.literal: Eight hundred fifty tons.
translations.idiomatic: 850 tons.

sentences.zh: 其屬於舊式者，巡洋艦五，曰通濟、一千九百頓。

translations.literal: Those belonging to the old type: five cruisers, named Tongji, one thousand nine hundred tons.
translations.idiomatic: Older types included five cruisers, beginning with the Tongji at 1,900 tons.

sentences.zh: 曰南琛、一千九百零五頓。

translations.literal: Named Nanchen, one thousand nine hundred five tons.
translations.idiomatic: The Nanchen, 1,905 tons.

sentences.zh: 曰鏡清、一千一百頓。

translations.literal: Named Jingqing, one thousand one hundred tons.
translations.idiomatic: The Jingqing, 1,100 tons.

sentences.zh: 曰保民、一千四百七十七頓。

translations.literal: Named Baomin, one thousand four hundred seventy-seven tons.
translations.idiomatic: The Baomin, 1,477 tons.

sentences.zh: 曰登瀛洲。

translations.literal: Named Dengyingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Dengyingzhou.

sentences.zh: 一千二百五十八頓。

translations.literal: One thousand two hundred fifty-eight tons.
translations.idiomatic: 1,258 tons.

sentences.zh: 水雷砲艦二，曰建威、曰建安。

translations.literal: Two mine gunboats named Jianwei and Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Two mine gunboats, the Jianwei and Jian.

sentences.zh: 各八百十七頓。

translations.literal: Each eight hundred seventeen tons.
translations.idiomatic: Each 817 tons.

sentences.zh: 砲艦二十，曰泰安、曰甘泉、曰廣玉、曰廣戌、曰靖海、曰廕洲海、曰並徵、曰海鏡清、曰廣金、曰廣己、曰廣庚、曰策電、曰第電、曰海長清、曰清海、曰鈞和、曰飛虎、曰靖遠、曰綏遠、曰鎮濤。

translations.literal: Twenty gunboats: Taian, Ganquan, Guangyu, Guangxu, Jinghai, Yinzhouhai, Bingzheng, Haijingqing, Guangjin, Guangji, Guang geng, Cedain, Didian, Haichangqing, Qinghai, Junhe, Feihu, Jingyuan, Suiyuan, and Zhentao.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty gunboats in all—the Taian, Ganquan, Guangyu, Guangxu, Jinghai, and fourteen others including the Jingyuan, Suiyuan, and Zhentao—listed by name in the register.

sentences.zh: 共一萬零八百二十七頓。

translations.literal: Totaling ten thousand eight hundred twenty-seven tons.
translations.idiomatic: Together 10,827 tons.

sentences.zh: 報知艦四，曰超武、曰琛航、曰元凱、曰伏波。

translations.literal: Four dispatch vessels: Chaowu, Chenhang, Yuankai, and Fubo.
translations.idiomatic: Four dispatch vessels: the Chaowu, Chenhang, Yuankai, and Fubo.

sentences.zh: 共五千一百七十七頓。

translations.literal: Totaling five thousand one hundred seventy-seven tons.
translations.idiomatic: Together 5,177 tons.

sentences.zh: 雷魚艇八，曰湖鵬、曰湖隼、曰湖鶚、曰湖鷹、曰辰、曰宿、曰列、曰張。

translations.literal: Eight torpedo boats: Hupeng, Hun, Hu'e, Huying, Chen, Su, Lie, and Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: Eight torpedo boats: the Hupeng, Hun, Hu'e, Huying, Chen, Su, Lie, and Zhang.

sentences.zh: 共一千頓。

translations.literal: Totaling one thousand tons.
translations.idiomatic: Together 1,000 tons.

sentences.zh: 新舊大小各艦凡五十五艘。

translations.literal: Old and new, large and small, fifty-five vessels in all.
translations.idiomatic: In all, fifty-five vessels old and new, large and small.
